Chickpea and Spinach Curry: chickpeas and spinach with a blend of Indian spices
assistant|slow_cooker_yogurt_ingredients: 1/2 gallon milk plus 1/4 cup plain yogurt with live cultures; optional sweetener, flavorings, or probiotic powder
assistant|slow_cooker_yogurt_heating: Heat milk on low for 2-3 hours until it reaches 180-185°F (82-85°C) to kill bacteria
assistant|slow_cooker_yogurt_cooling: Cool heated milk to 110-120°F (43-49°C), which takes about 1-2 hours, before adding the starter
assistant|slow_cooker_yogurt_incubation: Add starter culture, cover, wrap in a towel, and incubate 8-12 hours or overnight
assistant|slow_cooker_yogurt_storage: After incubation, chill the yogurt and store it in airtight containers in the refrigerator
assistant|greek_yogurt_tip: Strain yogurt through cheesecloth or a fine-mesh sieve to make thicker, creamier Greek yogurt
assistant|yogurt_temperature_rationale: Heating milk to 180-185°F kills unwanted bacteria and denatures proteins so cultures can thicken the milk
assistant|thermometer_recommendation: Recommends using a thermometer for accurate temperature control and consistent, safe yogurt results
assistant|no_thermometer_fallback: Without a thermometer, heat milk on low 2-3 hours until it simmers, then cool before adding starter
assistant|plant_based_cooking_tips: Use varied vegetables and grains; choose low-sodium canned beans and rinse them; add vinegar or lemon juice to enhance flavors
assistant|vegan_yogurt_base: Soy yogurt: classic vegan alternative; brands include Silk and So Delicious
Coconut yogurt: creamy and rich; brands include So Delicious, Coconut Bliss, and Coyo
Almond yogurt: low-calorie and low-fat; brands include Almond Breeze, Silk, and So Delicious
Cashew yogurt: creamy and indulgent; store-bought (So Delicious) or homemade
Oat yogurt: good for nut allergies; brands include Oatly and So Delicious
Rice yogurt: hypoallergenic and easy to digest; brands include Rice Dream and So Delicious
Hemp yogurt: high in protein and omega-3s; brands include Good Karma and Elmhurst 1925
Flax yogurt: low-calorie and high-fiber; brands include Good Karma or homemade
assistant|vegan_yogurt_buying_tip: Choose unflavored and unsweetened vegan yogurt varieties to control added sugars and flavorings
assistant|yogurt_flavoring_ideas: Flavorings: vanilla extract or bean, cinnamon, fruit (berries, mango, peaches), nutmeg, ginger, lemon, cocoa
assistant|yogurt_sweetener_ideas: Sweeteners: honey, maple syrup, coconut sugar, date syrup, monk fruit (use sparingly), stevia
assistant|yogurt_addin_ideas: Add-ins: granola, nuts or seeds (almonds, walnuts, chia, flax), cocoa nibs, dried fruit
assistant|cashew_soaking_method: Rinse 1 cup cashews and soak in water at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain and rinse again
assistant|cashew_blending_method: Blend soaked cashews with 1/2 cup fresh water on high speed about 2 minutes until smooth and creamy
assistant|cashew_yogurt_consistency_tips: Use about a 1:1 cashew-to-water ratio (less water for thicker yogurt); strain mixture; chill at least 2 hours to thicken
assistant|cashew_yogurt_culture_tip: Use a vegan yogurt starter or probiotic powder designed for plant-based yogurts; incubate 8-12 hours on low heat
assistant|straining_tool_cheesecloth: Cheesecloth gives high filtration and catches small particles but can be messy to squeeze
assistant|straining_tool_nut_milk_bag: Nut milk bags are designed for plant-based milks and catch particles well but can be pricey
assistant|straining_tool_fine_mesh_sieve: Fine-mesh sieve is easy to use and clean but may leave a slightly grainy texture
assistant|yogurt_thickening_tip: Add unflavored gelatin or pectin to the yogurt mixture before incubation for a thicker result
assistant|non_dairy_milk_yogurt_tip: Almond, soy, or coconut milk can be substituted for dairy milk to make non-dairy slow cooker yogurt
assistant|straining_hygiene_tip: Use a clean and sanitized straining tool when straining cashew milk to prevent contamination
assistant|straining_technique_tip: Squeeze the mixture through the straining tool to extract as much liquid as possible; twist cheesecloth and press nut milk bags gently
assistant|straining_tool_recommendation: Beginners making cashew milk get the best straining results with cheesecloth or a nut milk bag
